scraped.title: NASA’s new Moon plan is taking shape, but some big questions remain
scraped.description: We tend to have a lot of technical discussion and debate. That point will continue to be debated."
scraped.h1: NASA’s new Moon plan is taking shape, but some big questions remain
scraped.body_text:
“We tend to have a lot of technical discussion and debate. That point will continue to be debated.”

SpaceX’s successful recovery of its Starship rocket last weekend cleared a major hurdle on NASA’s path to the Moon, opening up possibilities for higher launch rates and an all-important, long-delayed orbital refueling demo next year.

For SpaceX’s purposes, Saturday’s mid-air rocket catch will help engineers learn how to rapidly reuse Starships. That should expedite SpaceX’s deployment of its newest generation of Starlink Internet satellites. NASA, meanwhile, believes a higher launch cadence will lead to faster learning as SpaceX develops a deep space version of Starship to ferry astronaut crews to the surface of the Moon.

Early next year, SpaceX plans to bring online a second Starship launch site at Kennedy Space Center, Florida. A second Starship factory is also under construction at Kennedy, joining SpaceX’s existing SpaceX production line at Starbase, Texas. With two launch sites, SpaceX will have the pieces in place to take the next leap with Starship.

The Starship refueling demonstration has slipped two years since late 2024, effectively a day-for-day delay as SpaceX ironed out technical problems with the vehicle. SpaceX may have turned a corner with Saturday’s first-ever catch of Starship at the launch tower.

There are other Starship lander tests coming next year. First will be NASA’s Artemis III mission, followed by an uncrewed Starship landing demonstration on the Moon. The former requires no orbital refueling, and the latter will need heaps of it.

Ars recently spoke with Steve Creech , the program manager for NASA’s Human Landing System. In this role, Creech oversees NASA’s contracts with SpaceX and Blue Origin to develop crew-rated lunar landers for Artemis.

For Artemis III, NASA will launch a four-man crew to low-Earth orbit on a Space Launch System rocket and an Orion spacecraft. Orion will first dock with Blue Origin’s Blue Moon lander for two days of tests, following its launch on a New Glenn rocket. The astronauts will open hatches and enter Blue Moon’s pressurized crew cabin to test the vehicle’s environmental control and life support systems.

Then, the astronauts will return to Orion and undock from Blue Moon to set up for a rendezvous and docking with SpaceX’s Starship in a slightly lower orbit, keeping it below most of SpaceX’s Starlink constellation. Orion will stay attached to Starship for just two hours, and the astronauts won’t enter the SpaceX vehicle.

NASA changed the plan for the Artemis III mission earlier this year, rerouting the flight plan from a lunar mission to a low-Earth orbit mission. This means the Artemis program’s first crewed lunar landing will be on Artemis IV, targeted to launch before the end of 2028.

So, why is Artemis III seemingly testing so much more with Blue Origin than with Starship? Creech told Ars a big reason is to maintain SpaceX’s focus on orbital refueling. Blue Origin no longer requires in-space refueling for Artemis landing missions. Also, SpaceX has extensive experience with life support systems with its Dragon crew spacecraft. Blue Origin has comparatively little.

“The bigger challenges for [SpaceX] were the prop transfer and getting to the uncrewed landing demo,” Creech said. “The thing that we’re going to learn more with Starship is, when we dock with Orion, they will have control of the attitude, control of the stack. That integrated stack control will be on the Starship side. So, with that huge of a vehicle, I think we’re going to learn more on that.

“With Blue, we’re going to have Orion control the stack for this mission,” Creech said. “When we get to a later mission, the Blue lander with fully loaded prop will have to control the stack. But with Blue, trying to mitigate risk, we’re going to have Orion do that.”

Artemis III will be Blue Origin’s first time flying a crew cabin for orbital spaceflight. Blue Origin has experience with suborbital space tourism, but those flights were brief and didn’t require the level of advanced life support necessary for longer durations. Blue Origin and NASA will emphasize those test objectives on Artemis III.

“I think SpaceX’s part was really, we need to focus on the docking,” Creech said. “If we added a crew cabin, that would slow us down on the other things and not add to what we’re already doing.”

The Starship on Artemis III will have a full complement of Raptor engines and a docking port on its nose. Blue Moon will not have any main engines when it links up with Orion on Artemis III, only a set of smaller thrusters for pointing control and minor maneuvers.

“With Blue, you don’t have a BE-7 engine, you don’t have the cryo tanks,” Creech said. “They’re representing the mass of the lander when it comes back from the surface because we think that’s the most critical case. But it does have the crew cabin.”

While there’s no Starship life support demonstration on Artemis III, NASA added a new milestone to SpaceX’s Moon lander contract to test parts of its crew cabin on the ground. The additional testing involves construction of a prototype crew compartment, called Cabin One, at SpaceX’s test site at Starbase, Texas.

NASA levied new test requirements on Blue Origin, too. The company plans to launch its first Blue Moon test mission early next year after a monthslong delay caused by a rocket explosion on Blue Origin’s launch pad in May. This version of Blue Moon, known as Mark 1, has a single hydrogen-fueled BE-7 main engine. Future human-rated landers from Blue Origin will have three.

“One of the things we added into the program in the last year is, we really felt like we needed a test of the three-engine configuration,” Creech said. The hotfire test of the three-engine Blue Moon propulsion unit will occur inside a vacuum chamber at NASA’s In-Space Propulsion Facility in Ohio.

This year’s Artemis shakeup did more than change the flight plan for Artemis III. Engineers also altered the architecture for subsequent lunar landing missions. The updated plans will make life easier for teams working on Starship and Blue Moon. That’s not necessarily the case for Orion .

“Our previous architecture for both these landers required a 90-day loiter in lunar orbit for Orion to arrive,” Creech said. “That was something that, for both of these landers, drove a lot of complexity, and a lot of it made the lander job really hard.”

The new concept of operations does away with some of that complexity, according to NASA.

“One of the things we changed was that 90-day loiter,” Creech said. “SpaceX, they solved it by saying let’s do an Earth orbit rendezvous with Orion, and take Orion to the Moon. For both Blue Origin and SpaceX, we have updated their requirements to a four-day surface day initially. Before, our initial missions were six-and-a-half days.”

The six-and-a-half day surface stay was baked into the Artemis architecture because the Orion spacecraft was originally planned to settle into a long, looping path around the Moon, called a near rectilinear halo orbit. This orbit was predicated by the expected location of NASA’s now-canceled Gateway lunar space station. That, in turn, was driven by Orion’s inability to reach an orbit closer to the Moon.

Now, instead of rendezvousing with Starship near the Moon on landing missions, Orion will link up with Starship in high-Earth orbit. From there, Starship will propel it toward the Moon.

What’s still not clear, however, is whether SpaceX will have to refuel Starship at an altitude somewhere above low-Earth orbit. A graphic presented by Jeremy Parsons , NASA’s Artemis program manager, last month illustrated this possibility with a “final tanking orbit” before Starship docks with Orion in high-Earth orbit.

“We’re still working that out,” Creech said. “We’re making progress, but where we actually rendezvous with Orion is still in trade, so that’s why you saw a little bit of fuzziness there.”

For missions using Blue Moon, the lander will connect with Orion in orbit around the Moon. Blue Origin’s updated plans do away with the requirement for in-space refueling but will still require four launches of the company’s New Glenn rocket, one for the Blue Moon lander itself and three with transfer stages to boost it out of Earth orbit to the Moon.

A new stretched Centaur upper stage for the Space Launch System should give the rocket energy to send Orion to low-lunar orbit , which it could not reach with the current version of SLS. NASA has not determined if the new Centaur exploration stage will be ready in time for Artemis IV. If not, Artemis IV could fly with the last of NASA’s in-stock SLS upper stages.

NASA is also waiting to decide which lander to use on Artemis IV. In either case, two of Orion’s four astronauts will transfer into the landers for final descent to the lunar surface for a four-day stay, followed by takeoff and return to Orion.

Starship and Blue Moon must each complete an uncrewed landing demonstration before a crew lunar mission. The landing demos are targeted for late 2027 or early 2028, Creech said, but they won’t necessarily test everything crews will need when they head for the lunar south pole.

Starship’s elevator, for example, is not part of SpaceX’s uncrewed landing demonstration. Engineers will use a test lab at Marshall Space Flight Center in Alabama to check the elevator’s performance in a simulated lunar environment.

NASA did not initially require SpaceX or Blue Origin to prove their landers could take off from the Moon before a crew mission. Government officials later added the lunar takeoff requirement for each company’s uncrewed landing demos.

For now, NASA is leaving the details of the uncrewed takeoff demo up to SpaceX and Blue Origin. During Apollo, NASA’s lunar lander never landed on the Moon before Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin descended to the Sea of Tranquility. NASA did, however, fly a dress rehearsal around the Moon on Apollo 10 that included a test of the lunar module’s landing abort capability.

“Where we are today is, Blue will land and then do a full ascent back to the rendezvous point with Orion,” Creech said. “With SpaceX. They will land, they will take off again, get to main stage on the engines, and then they will do another landing on the surface.”

That could change. Today’s plan gives SpaceX two shots at proving Starship can safely land on the Moon, but it comes with tradeoffs.

“When I came into the program, I was like, ‘Why are we not going all the way to the rendezvous point?’” said Creech, who took over as HLS program manager in 2025. “Some of my key people felt strongly we would get more out of the way we’re doing it now. There are others that have different opinions… We tend to have a lot of technical discussion and debate. That point will continue to be debated.”

For Starship, orbital refueling remains the key to the Moon. SpaceX’s propellant transfer demonstration will involve two Starships, one launched from Florida and another from Texas, docking together in low-Earth orbit and transferring a “meaningful” amount of propellant from one ship to the other, Creech said.

“The first quarter of next year, we will see a long-awaited propellant transfer test from SpaceX, where they launch two Starships in pretty close proximity, actually dock, and transfer, we’re calling it a meaningful amount, of propellant,” Creech told Ars. “That is going to be a big learning point if they pull that off, because their architecture depends on propellant aggregation and multiple propellant flights.”

The propellant transfer test will mark the first time one spacecraft has offloaded a significant quantity of cryogenic propellants —in this case, methane and liquid oxygen —onto another vehicle in space. It is the culmination of decades of government and commercial research on cryogenic orbital refueling. The results will tell engineers how much of the propellant will be lost from boil-off during the transfer.

That is one reason why there’s still so much ambiguity about how many Starship refueling tankers SpaceX will need to launch to give the Starship lunar lander enough gas to fly to the Moon. Without refueling, Starships are restricted to flights in low-Earth orbit.

The low end of the estimate for Starship tankers is six to eight refueling flights to support a Starship lunar mission. Those numbers come from Elon Musk, SpaceX’s founder and CEO, and fall below NASA’s own conservative planning figure of 20 refueling launches . Musk’s figures hinge on future Starship upgrades to reach the vehicle’s full potential. SpaceX’s goal is to get Starship’s lift capacity up to 100 to 200 metric tons of payload to low-Earth orbit. Today’s version of Starship, known as Starship V3, is still far short of 100 metric tons of payload capacity.

For context, a Starship carries 1,600 metric tons of propellant with its tanks full. Refueling flights using future fully-optimized Starships might be able to fill those tanks with as few as six tankers. That is not the case today.

SpaceX is working on a taller, heavier Starship called Starship V4. It will fly with nine Raptor engines, an upgrade over the six-engine variant flying today. In 2025, Musk said Starship V4’s first launch was targeted for 2027. There hasn’t been a recent update to the schedule for Starship V4.

The initial Artemis lunar missions will use Starship V3, Creech said.

Even as the fall-out for Nvidia over Jensen Huang’s alleged honey-trap scandal is still unfolding, Silicon Valley has yet to reckon with a new reality: many more people among them are at risk.

“Nobody briefs founders on counterintelligence,” Aaron Brown, a former senior CIA officer and current founder of the software company Lumbra, told TechCrunch.

That’s because historically honey traps have been associated with politicians, the military and national intelligence — the people “behind clearances and a workforce trained to expect an approach,” from spies and other attackers.

But now many of the most valuable secrets “sit inside companies building chips, models, and infrastructure,” Brown says, adding that a spy “wants what the CEO can touch. The roadmap, the export decisions, the customer list, who gets the technology. The CEO is the shortest path to all of it.”

Huang has been accused of falling for just such a honey trap by having an affair with Alice Huang. She’s a former executive of a Singapore neocloud who’s been accused of being a Chinese spy and of smuggling billions of dollars’ worth of restricted Nvidia chips into China.

After the Huang allegations broke, jokes flooded the internet about which tech CEO will be next, but it’s not just CEOs and founders who are at risk. The WSJ reported that OpenAI started warning its employees about outsiders trying to cozy up to them in search of company secrets. Anyone with access to sensitive information — from board members to executive assistants — can be the target of a honey-trap.

And typically, the attackers aren’t lovers. Friendship is actually the oldest honest trap scheme around, Brown said.

Honey traps gain access to their targets as investors, customers, recruiters, and consultancies. Their requests look legitimate on paper and don’t need their targets to fall in love. “They need you to feel comfortable talking,” Brown said. “They last longer because nobody’s looking.”

What’s interesting, too, is the irony. So many tech founders are moving to automate and digitize so much of human life and yet remain vulnerable to the oldest bug around, a person who preys on the human need to be understood by others.

“Why fight through a firewall when you can get close to the person who can open doors, influence decisions, or make requests nobody wants to question?” Perry Carpenter, a cybercrimologist and chief deception strategist at KnowBe4, told TechCrunch.

Once targets realize they have been compromised, the threat can escalate: attackers now have a means of blackmail.

Another irony: AI has made honey trapping much easier and cheaper. Planning a scheme used to take months or years of research, crafting a persona, knowing the target, and executing a plan. These days, it’s easy to use AI to research a target, generate fake social profiles, fake backgrounds, even fake voice calls.

“AI can help sustain an entire fictional backstory,” Carpenter said. “The technology helps set the stage, but the deception ultimately plays out through human relationships.”

The AI industry “became a national security industry faster than its culture caught up,” Brown said.

“Part of being honey trapped is not knowing,” he added. “It doesn’t feel like manipulation. It feels genuine, even lucky.”

Carpenter said a good first step is looking for unusual patterns. Note, for instance, “coincidental encounters that happen a little too often,” he said. There are also obvious signs, like persistent curiosity about work and colleagues, or requesting secrecy about meeting up, and pressing for introductions or information.

Bigger red flags include if someone’s requests are getting bigger, pushing the boundaries of what you usually would be uncomfortable doing. “A simple gut check,” Brown said. “Would this person still be around if you lost your job tomorrow?”

It also helps to try and understand when emotions might be influencing a decision. Carpenter suggests putting up a clear boundary between one’s personal and professional life. Within companies, it also helps to “eliminate executive exceptionalism,” he said, the idea that the rules don’t apply to people in power at the company.

Brown added that company culture plays another role, too: are employees comfortable with raising concerns, challenging unusual requests, and escalating possible threats? “One of the most dangerous security cultures is one where nobody feels comfortable questioning the CEO,” Carpenter said.

“Founders need to take risks, and they need to explore business opportunities,” Brown said. “Paranoia doesn’t help. Recognizing you’re a target does.”

Spotify founder Daniel Ek is backing Europa Fusion, a stealthy fusion power startup founded by an AI researcher who is taking a different approach to developing a fusion power plant.

The U.K.-based startup was founded in February, though sources told TechCrunch that the founder, Nantas Nardelli, has been working on the idea for longer. The people asked not to be identified because the information isn’t public. Bloomberg first reported Ek’s backing of Europa Fusion.

Nardelli has extensive experience in the AI world, having previously worked at Google DeepMind, Facebook AI Research, and Microsoft Research Cambridge. Recently, he was head of machine learning at Pacific Fusion , the fusion power startup based in Fremont, California.

Pacific Fusion recently broke ground on a demonstration facility in New Mexico. Like most fusion startups of its size , Pacific Fusion leans heavily on physical devices to test its theories and improve its simulations.

Nardelli apparently didn’t agree with the focus on hardware, instead thinking that fusion startups should invest in a more simulation- and data-heavy approach, a source familiar with his thinking told TechCrunch.

Like Pacific Fusion, Europa Fusion will pursue a pulsed-power approach to fusion. Pulsed-power reactors use massive, perfectly timed surges of electrical current to compress fuel targets until the atoms inside fuse and release energy.

Fusion power has the potential to be a significant energy source in the coming decades, but to date, no one has built a power plant capable of supplying electricity to the grid. If fusion power becomes commercially viable, though, it could possibly be a significant source of carbon-free power that draws on nearly limitless fuel supplies. The technology also has the potential to alleviate concerns about AI’s energy consumption.

Fusion’s ability to generate electricity without exacerbating climate change apparently drove Nardelli’s pivot from AI.

“My original background is in electronics and control engineering,” he wrote on his website . “I used to build robots for a living. One day I’ll be back to that, but it’s time to fix climate change for good.”

It’s a big week for Levent Alpöge: The mathematician saw his employer, Anthropic, become the first publicly traded frontier AI lab. He also appears to have solved one of the most important problems in mathematics.

“The precise timing is horrible,” he wrote in an essay announcing his findings and describing how he messaged Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei last Sunday night to ask how to announce that he had found a Lean-compilable solution to the Riemann Hypothesis, which dates back to 1859 and is among the Millennium Prize math problems.

The Hypothesis conjectures that there is a hidden structure underlying the appearance of prime numbers. If the claimed result holds true, we’re entering sublime-mysteries-of-the-universe territory.

Maybe the best way to understand how exciting this is to the mathematics community is to watch the experts puzzling through the result in a chat on Zulip . Mathematicians like Chris Birkbeck, a number theorist at the University of East Anglia, are posting thoughts like this …

The cohomology bound is proved by what looks like an automorphy-lifting argument. It genuinely uses the existence of Galois representations attached to regular algebraic, polarized cuspidal automorphic representations of GL_n over CM fields, along with base change, Jacquet–Shalika, Clozel’s purity, Bernstein–Zelevinsky, the main theorem of CM, Deligne–Ribet and more.

For my part, I tapped out of mathematics at college calculus, so I can’t help decode exactly what that means.

But that comment was followed by 20 readers reacting 🤯.

It will be a while before the mathematics community feels like it has a handle on the proof, but most appear confident that the formalized Lean result will hold. Lean is an an open source language that essentially helps verify mathematical proofs.

Alpöge appeared in his essay to feel a bit guilty about releasing the proof without a truly human-intelligible explanation, but his obsession with the problem since childhood made him feel he “could not live” if he waited to release the finding.

Alpöge described a “stream-of-consciousness jaunt through the experience of finding all the pieces of the argument through incredible confusion with Claude” with more than a hint of AI euphoria, describing how the model “flew, and danced, and sparkled near that finish line.”

However, for all that action to mean anything, we’ll have to wait for humans to be able to understand the result and explain it to each other, something Alpöge has committed to pursue.

Alpöge and a collaborator, NYU mathematician Tristan Buckmaster, also released another important proof related to the Navier-Stokes equations, problems that helped kick off the race between frontier labs and mathematicians to solve outstanding problems this summer.

Meanwhile, Ravi Vakil, a Stanford professor and the president of the American Mathematics Association, posted a proof of the General Riemann Hypothesis written by Stanford postdoc Alessandro Masullo, noting that “it is all human, with no AI. The hope was to bring Alessandro to Stanford for a year to polish the writing and then announce it after running it by enough people. Now it seems best to put out the current draft.”

In a brief introduction to his proof, which he said is the result of 12 years of work, Masullo wrote that “if any message at all this work is meant to send to the mathematician who feels discouraged by the pace and tone of the current climate, it is this: we are still here. We are very much alive. We are not going anywhere.”

scraped.author: Kevin Breuninger
scraped.h1: Trump vows to stop U.S. companies from building data centers abroad, threatens 'tremendous tax'
scraped.body_text:
President Donald Trump on Friday said U.S. companies will be banned from building data centers in other countries and will face a "tremendous tax" penalty if they do so.

"We're going to fight very hard for the data centers," Trump said at a White House press conference before announcing the new policy — which apparently came as news to his own staff.

"I don't know if that's a breaking story," Trump said. "I haven't even said that to my people. But I'm telling them now they're here."

Trump's latest push for more data-center construction in the U.S. came despite Americans repeatedly stating — and showing with their votes — that they dislike the structures.

CNBC's All-America Economic Survey found that 64% of registered voters opposed an AI data center within 10 miles of their home, while just 13% of respondents said they would support one.

If Trump follows through on his threat to clamp down on overseas data center construction, he will have to contend with the fact that numerous U.S. tech giants — including Alphabet , Amazon , Microsoft , Meta and Oracle — have already built them in other countries.

International expansion represents a growth opportunity for the top cloud infrastructure providers, which want to serve clients from data centers that are nearby, sometimes to meet regulatory requirements.

Trump said Friday, however, that if companies want to continue building the centers outside the U.S., "they can, but we're going to put a tremendous tax on them."

"We have a lot of places that want them badly, and they're great places. They have energy, and they have everything. They're tremendous assets," Trump said.

Representatives at cloud providers Amazon , Google , Microsoft and Oracle did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Trump's remarks came a day after Trump met with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in China for a trilateral summit that appeared to produce few concrete deliverables on an array of pressing global issues.

Xi "congratulated me on how well we're doing" in artificial intelligence, Trump said, using his preferred term "super intelligence," which he said the Chinese president also likes better.

— CNBC's Jordan Novet and Annie Palmer contributed reporting.

scraped.title: Nvidia stock plunges 12%, rides longest weekly losing streak since 2008 financial crisis
scraped.description: Once the most valuable company in the world, Nvidia now ranks third behind Apple and Microsoft.
scraped.author: Kif Leswing
scraped.h1: Nvidia stock plunges 12%, rides longest weekly losing streak since 2008 financial crisis
scraped.body_text:
In this article

The last time Wall Street was this down on Nvidia the chipmaker's flagship product was the GeForce graphics processor for high-end PC video games, and markets were reeling from the global financial crisis.

Nvidia shares fell 12% on Friday, sliding for a seventh straight day as investors grew increasingly concerned about life after co-founder Jensen Huang . The stock is poised to close lower for a seventh consecutive week, the longest such stretch since 2008.

Shares of Nvidia are down 44% over the period, pushing the company's market cap down by $2.5 trillion. The stock is now trading at around 9.3 times forward earnings, while Advanced Micro Devices is valued at 29 times profit for the next 12 months.

On Friday, Reuters reported that the Securities and Exchange Commission is exploring potential accounting issues at Nvidia, pushing the stock down further.

Once the most valuable company, now, at a market cap of $3.1 trillion, Nvidia is fourth behind Apple and Microsoft and Alphabet .

Nvidia is reeling from the removal of Huang, who resigned on Nov. 12, after multiple reported affairs , including one with a Chinese businesswoman who was allegedly a spy.

Harvey Jones, Nvidia's newly appointed board chair, said earlier this week that Huang had resigned after "disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company's code of conduct, standards and cultural norms."

But the chipmaker's losing streak started before Nvidia was thrown into crisis as investors worried over the sustainability of the AI buildout, particularly after the midterm elections, and emerging competition in AI chips from Google and AMD.

Even a better-than-expected earnings report, which included an increase to fiscal 2028 guidance, didn't stem the selling. Interim CEO Colette Kress, the company's longtime CFO, projected revenue growth next fiscal year of 75%, and said that customers aren't going anywhere.

On Tuesday's earnings call with analysts, Kress signed off by saying, "we've got this." In a company meeting the next day, executives told staff that it was moving its yearly review process, which can come with more stock, from March to December.

For investors, one major question is whether Nvidia can continue to innovate and sustain its commanding lead in the AI chip market without its visionary leader. Almost the entire company now is built around the AI trade, a phenomenon that began taking hold just four years ago with the launch of OpenAI's ChatGPT.

Before that, Nvidia's primary business was selling graphics cards used for video games. In mid-2008, the last time the stock was this deep into a weekly losing streak, Nvidia was generating less than $1 billion per quarter. Now it pulls in more than $1 billion per day. At the time, the entire market was in freefall due to the worst financial crisis since the Great Depression.

scraped.title: A massive bearish trade just happened in the chip stocks
scraped.description: Options traders place big bets that semiconductor stocks have further to fall
scraped.author: Oliver Renick
scraped.h1: Options Action
scraped.body_text:
In this article

So much for buying the dip. As the S&P 500 entered correction territory and the Nasdaq-100 flirted with bear-market territory, down 19% from highs as of midday Friday, the single biggest options trade of the day was a near $100-million bet that the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) has a long way more to fall. Around 12:30 E.T., someone spent $93 million buying 20,000 380-strike puts expiring Sep. 17, 2027, according to trading data reviewed by SpotGamma and Volland, options-analytics platforms that both show the trade as a likely opening position, with volume exceeding existing open interest in the contract. The trade bets that the index will fall below $380, a nearly 8% decline from its current level. The SMH is off 40% from its recent all-time highs.

"That trade stands out big-time," wrote Jason DeLorenzo, founder and owner of Volland. "It is either a hedge or speculative, but either way it isn't a vote of confidence." The puts were bought for $46.50 a piece, an arguably expensive choice for a downside bet with volatility in the ETF trading at 70.

"You're paying a metric ton of Vega for that thing," added SpotGamma's Brent Kochuba, referring to the contract's sensitivity to changes in volatility of the underlying chip ETF. "Maybe they were a forced buyer, or maybe they're actually selling this, which can still be the case even though the price shows it happening closer to the ask."

The semiconductor index headed for a 9% drop this week alone.

The S&P 500 and the Dow were on track ​for a correction on Friday as Anthropic shares retreated after a blockbuster debut, dashing hopes that the listing would stabilize an AI trade ‌already shaken by valuation concerns.

Both benchmarks were down 10 per cent from their record closing highs. An index falling 10 per cent or more below its record high on a close-to-close basis is called a correction.

The IPO, together with Nvidia’s earnings this week, was seen as a key ​gauge of whether confidence in AI-linked stocks could recover after weeks of selling pressure due to concerns about elevated borrowing costs, regulatory ​uncertainty following Democrats’ victory in the US midterm elections and the departure of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.

“Anthropic is ⁠so critical in assessing the overall market landscape in the end,” said Gina Martin Adams, chief market strategist at HB Wealth.

“You absolutely need to ​continue to see adoption and some form of price discovery as to what companies and individuals will be willing to pay for this technology … until ​you get to a point where the market feels a little bit more confident that we’ve adequately priced it.”

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index shed 8.6 per cent to a seven-month low. Nvidia fell 7 per cent to its lowest level since June 2025 and was heading for its longest weekly losing streak since 2008.

Among hyperscalers, Amazon was down 2 per cent and Meta declined ​3.6 per cent, while Alphabet gained 1 per cent. Amazon and Alphabet are among Anthropic’s biggest investors.

Neocloud firms CoreWeave and Nebius also dropped over 10 per cent each.

The main ​US stock indexes were on track for their steepest weekly decline since April 2025, when US President Donald Trump announced Liberation Day tariffs.

Six of the 11 major S&P ‌500 sectors ⁠were lower, with the benchmark heading for its longest losing streak since February 2020.

The tech sector led losses with a 4.5 per cent drop, while industrials and consumer discretionary slipped over 1.5 per cent each.

Healthcare stocks were up 0.8 per cent after four straight sessions of losses.

At 12:11 p.m. ET, the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 206.90 points, or 0.42 per cent, to 48,890.16, the S&P 500 lost 135.15 points, or 1.88 per cent, to 7,040.68 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 789.22 points, or 3.30 per cent, ​to 23,091.82.

Federal Reserve ​Governor Lisa Cook on Friday said ⁠the US central bank’s current policy rate is not high enough to deal with inflation levels she views with “great concern.”

Markets are pricing in a 98.2 per cent chance of an interest rate hike from the central bank at its ​next meeting in December, according to CME Group’s FedWatch tool.

A final University of Michigan survey showed consumer ​sentiment rose to 51.5 ⁠in November from 48.0 in October.

Next week’s personal consumption expenditures (PCE) figures will provide further clarity on the Fed’s monetary policy path after a hotter-than-expected October inflation report last week.

Among other movers, Intuit shares fell 8.7 per cent after the company cut its annual revenue growth forecast and agreed to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for about $3.68 ⁠billion, five ​years after acquiring it for nearly three times as much.

Declining issues outnumbered advancers ​by a 2.04-to-1 ratio on the NYSE and by a 2.8-to-1 ratio on the Nasdaq.

The S&P 500 posted 3 new 52-week highs and 13 new lows while the Nasdaq Composite ​recorded 12 new highs and 626 new lows.

scraped.h1: UN court finds Myanmar guilty of Rohingya genocide in landmark judgement
scraped.body_text:
Instructions:

6 comments

The UN judge will probably sentence Myanmar to a million Muslim “asylum seekers” and 100000 more a year for the next five years.

The problem is that they tossed away their credibility long ago

There are many leaders in many countries that should be brought to justice for genocides and yet none are. Putin flaunts his genocide and it is accepted among world leaders when he should be brought up on charges of crimes against humanity and refused entry to any other country!

White genocide is happening over the entire globe

Good, now do Israel next.

How much longer do Canadian tax dollars have to keep funding the farce known as the U.N? Lots of dollars wasted on this court case that means nothing because no one will face any punishment, and won’t lead to free elections.

Myanmar’s government on Friday dismissed a landmark judgment by the United Nations’ top court finding the country guilty of genocide against its Rohingya minority as “unfair,” while opponents called upon the international community to follow through to ensure justice is done.

Khine Khine Soe, spokeswoman for President Min Aung Hlaing, noted that judges had only voted nine-to-six on Thursday to find Myanmar committed genocide against the Muslim minority Rohingya in a brutal 2017 military operation.

“Not all 15 judges agreed with the decision,” she told reporters in the capital Naypyitaw. “So it was not a decision made unanimously. I would say that it was unfair.”

The ruling by The Hague-based International Court of Justice, or ICJ, was the first time the court has ruled that a state committed genocide. Myanmar’s government has denied the allegation, claiming it acted against insurgents in the 2017 military operation in northern Rakhine state.

The case focused on the military’s so-called “clearance operations” in Rakhine state in 2017 when the democratically-elected government of Aung San Suu Kyi was in power. Min Aung Hlaing, who was commander in chief at the time, seized power from Suu Kyi in 2021 and has since consolidated his control of the government, being elected president earlier this year in a vote critics said was neither free nor fair.

The country is now embroiled in a bloody civil war, with pro-democracy and other militias fighting against the military.

The militant Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army, or ARSA, whose attacks in 2017 against government outposts in Rakhine State were the trigger for the Myanmar military’s devastating crackdown, called the ruling an “important step towards justice” in a statement on Telegram.

The court said that evidence showed Myanmar forces killed about 10,000 Rohingya in the campaign in which the military was accused of committing mass rapes and killings, and razing thousands of homes.

About 1.2 million Rohingya refugees now live in Bangladesh, primarily in crowded camps across Cox’s Bazar district, where they endure harsh conditions marked by fire hazards, infectious diseases, monsoon landslides, inadequate sanitation and strict work restrictions.

Nay San Lwin, an activist with the Arakan Rohingya National Council, who now lives outside Myanmar, said this was just the “first victory on our path to our final one: returning to our homeland and living there in peace and dignity.”

“Without action and support from the international community, the court’s order will remain only a declaration,” he told The Associated Press. “Every country must help in whatever way it can.”

ARSA stressed that refugees have to be allowed to return home safely and that those responsible must face justice.

“We call upon the United Nations and the international community to ensure that Myanmar complies with the Court’s judgment and that justice is not left on paper,” the group said in a statement signed by “Ustad Khalid Junun,” described as its chief of general staff.

The Rohingya Solidarity Organization, or RSO, a rival militant group, issued a similar statement.

ARSA and the RSO have been marginalized since 2017, by suppression from Myanmar authorities and infighting. They are now involved in three-way fighting in Rakhine, where the Arakan Army, a Buddhist-dominated group seeking autonomy for the state, is battling the Myanmar military but has also been accused of targeting the Rohingya.

The Arakan Army did not respond to a request for comment on the court decision.

In its ruling, the court ordered Myanmar to commit to allowing Rohingya “safe, voluntary and dignified return to their place of residence.” It also ordered Myanmar to investigate, prosecute and punish people found to have committed genocidal acts and to pay compensation to Rohingya. The amount will be decided in later court proceedings.

Khine Khine Soe did not address those demands, but it was widely seen as unlikely that Myanmar would comply. She said Myanmar would reply once it reviewed the lengthy court documents.

“Since this is an international case, we will make our position known,” she said.

She also questioned the court’s jurisdiction to impose conditions, and referenced a declaration on Thursday by U.S. President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese leader Xi Jinping at their historic trilateral meeting in China, in which they said “ the International Criminal Court and other similar bodies must not abuse their jurisdiction.”

“The main point is that the ICC and similar international institutions should not abuse their judicial authority,” Khine Khine Soe told reporters. “Given that three (of the) world’s leading nations have issued statements on this matter … you can think about it for yourselves.”

China’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said Friday that while the country stood ready to “play a constructive role in advancing the repatriation of displaced people from Rakhine state, ”China has concerns over issues such as jurisdiction overreach and broad interpretations, and we believe such practices are not conducive to resolving disputes.”

Myanmar’s shadow National Unity Government, the main organization coordinating opposition to military rule in Myanmar since the 2021 army takeover, welcomed the ICJ ruling, saying it respected the authority of the court and its judgment.

It also stressed that the pursuit of justice for the Rohingya must be accompanied by efforts to end the military’s ongoing violence against civilians across Myanmar.

A cyberattack carried out with artificial intelligence targeted the European Union in October, an official in Brussels said on Thursday, and some of the bloc’s digital tools remain offline.

The official did not elaborate on the cyberattack, or say who could have been behind it. It was the first time the 27-member bloc reported a cyberattack using an AI tool.

“AI-assisted tools can be used and especially misused to detect vulnerabilities,” said Thomas Regnier, spokesperson for the European Commission, the executive body of the 27-nation EU.

“Indeed we can confirm that this was done with AI tools,” he added. “We have seen many global cyberattacks recently, and of course no one is immune to this.”

Regnier said the EU first detected the incident on Oct. 22 and that authorities launched an investigation while also imposing “preventative measures.”

Politico first reported the incidents. The news site said the attack lasted at least 10 days and affected translation and reimbursement tools as well as databases used for salaries and timesheets. Regnier declined to confirm that report.

“We temporarily took down several applications, and most of them have since then been restored,” Regnier said. So far, however, Regnier said that “we have not detected any evidence of a data breach affecting commission staff as a whole.”

The EU agency CERT-EU oversees the digital security of the bloc’s various institutions, which all together employ about 40,000 people just in Brussels.

scraped.title: HK doctor found guilty over fraudulently issuing Covid-19 vaccine exemptions
scraped.description: A Hong Kong doctor accused of fraudulently issuing around 3,700 Covid-19 vaccine exemption certificates during the pandemic has been found guilty of accessing a computer with dishonest intent.
scraped.author: Hillary Leung
scraped.h1: Hong Kong doctor found guilty over fraudulently issuing over 3,700 Covid-19 vaccine exemptions
scraped.body_text:
Hong Kong Free Press HKFP

Hong Kong news, breaking updates – 100% Independent, impartial, non-profit

A Hong Kong doctor accused of fraudulently issuing around 3,700 Covid-19 vaccine exemption certificates during the pandemic has been found guilty of accessing a computer with dishonest intent.

Tai Kong-shing received his verdict at the District Court on Friday after pleading not guilty. He was also found guilty of money laundering.

A volunteer at the clinic, Kriselle Young, was also found guilty of accessing a computer with dishonest intent.

According to the prosecution, the pair conspired to defraud the Health Bureau between February and September 2022 by dishonestly claiming that some patients were medically unfit to receive the Covid-19 vaccine.

Tai handed out 3,751 vaccine exemptions, charging between HK$1,000 and HK$4,000 each.

During the Covid-19 pandemic, members of the public were required to be vaccinated to access restaurants, gyms and other specified premises.

Delivering the verdict, Judge Ernest Lin said the clinic made use of the “unreasonable, unscientific fears” of “selfish” members of the public for commercial gain.

He said Tai, as a doctor, had sufficient medical knowledge to understand the Hospital Authority’s guidelines. Yet he gave out vaccine exemptions simply because his patients were paying him, rather than after assessing their medical conditions.

Lin said that Young was not a trained medical practitioner, but that she introduced patients to the clinic and allocated work to the nurses. She knowingly assisted Tai in inputting false information, the judge added.

During an undercover operation that led to the pair’s arrest, three police officers disguised themselves as patients and visited Tai’s clinic to request Covid-19 vaccine exemptions, saying they were afraid to get the jab.

Tai issued the exemptions, including one for an officer’s son who was not at the appointment.

Tai testified during the trial that he did not blindly give out exemptions to patients, saying they had suffered from gastritis, chest pain, asthma and other conditions that made them unfit for the vaccine.

Young also testified, saying that she was a volunteer at the clinic and that she trusted Tai’s judgement. She said she never thought that he had abused the issuing of exemption certificates.

When asked by the prosecution about a WhatsApp message she had sent to a patient reading “don’t worry, [it’ll] definitely be issued,” Young denied reassuring the patient that they would be able to obtain an exemption certificate, saying instead that she was comforting them.

scraped.title: Alleged UK spy for HK died by suicide ahead of trial, British jury rules
scraped.description: A former British marine who was charged with spying for Hong Kong has died by suicide, a UK jury has found. Matthew Trickett took his own life after a public services firm failed to locate him and fit his electronic tag.
scraped.author: Tom Grundy
scraped.h1: Alleged UK spy for Hong Kong died by suicide ahead of trial, British jury rules
scraped.body_text:
Hong Kong Free Press HKFP

Hong Kong news, breaking updates – 100% Independent, impartial, non-profit

A former British marine who was charged with spying for Hong Kong died by suicide, a UK jury has found. Matthew Trickett took his own life after a public services firm failed to locate him and fit his electronic tag.

In May 2024, the 37-year-old was found dead in Maidenhead’s Grenfell Park. He had been arrested and charged under the UK’s National Security Act weeks earlier for allegedly assisting Hong Kong’s intelligence service.

Trickett – a Home Office immigration officer – was seen attempting self-harm in his cell while in detention, but was released on bail two days later.

On multiple occasions, Serco – which provides judicial and correctional services to the UK government – “failed to take reasonable steps” to locate his address, the jury at Reading Coroner’s Court found on Wednesday, according to the BBC.

Peter Wai and Bill Yuen, Trickett’s co-defendants, were jailed for 10 and eight years, respectively, in June for assisting Hong Kong’s foreign intelligence service. Wai, a former UK Border Force officer, was convicted of conducting a “shadow policing” operation upon the orders of Yuen, an office manager at the Hong Kong Economic and Trade Office in London.

The two British-Chinese dual nationals targeted Hong Kong pro-democracy protesters living in the UK. Hong Kong denied any link to the apparent spying .

In full: Explainer: Why UK authorities arrested 3 men linked to Hong Kong’s trade office

Among those the pair were said to have surveilled was activist Nathan Law, who is wanted by national security police in Hong Kong with a HK$1 million bounty on his head.

Trickett had penned a final letter to his family dated May 23, 2024 – the day before he was due to appear in court. “Upon learning that police were trying to locate him and fearing he would be arrested and taken back to custody, Matt brought his plan forward and re-dated his letter to May 19,” the jury reportedly said.

One of his friends told the court last week that Trickett, who had worked as a private security consultant since 2013, feared the “humiliation” of a possible conviction and had warned he might kill himself.

Senior coroner Heidi Connor said Serco had yet to carry out an internal investigation, adding that the company must “improve its systems” to mitigate the risk of more people dying. A simple Google Maps search could have averted what she nevertheless said was a “very rare” scenario.

Following Wednesday’s ruling, a spokesperson for Serco said the company would review the coroner’s report and recommendation.

scraped.title: HK man jailed for life for murdering yoga instructor ex-girlfriend
scraped.description: A Hong Kong man has been sentenced to life behind bars for murdering his yoga instructor ex-girlfriend by stabbing her inside a luxury hotel room four years ago.
scraped.author: Hans Tse
scraped.h1: Hong Kong man jailed for life for murdering yoga instructor ex-girlfriend in luxury hotel
scraped.body_text:
Hong Kong Free Press HKFP

Hong Kong news, breaking updates – 100% Independent, impartial, non-profit

A Hong Kong man has been sentenced to life behind bars for murdering his yoga instructor ex-girlfriend by stabbing her inside a luxury hotel room four years ago.

Alex Lo, 32, was given life imprisonment at the High Court on Friday, a day after being unanimously found guilty of murder by a seven-member jury comprising five men and two women.

He was convicted of murdering yoga instructor Aqua Chow between June 29 and June 30, 2022, at the Ritz-Carlton in West Kowloon.

In a mitigation letter, Lo apologised to Chow, her mother and friends, and said that he only pleaded not guilty and stood trial on the advice of an unnamed lawyer, according to court news outlet The Witness.

“If there were a fixed penalty of 20 or 30 years in jail, I believe I would have pleaded guilty at the earliest stage,” he wrote in Chinese. Under Hong Kong law, adults convicted of murder face mandatory life imprisonment, with no sentencing discount for pleading guilty.

Lo said he had never hoped to publicly disclose the details of his relationship with Chow, adding that she was his “most beloved woman.”

“I used the wrong way to love in this relationship and I am willing to bear the consequences,” he wrote.

Judge Anthony Kwok, however, found that Lo only demonstrated slight remorse, noting he sought to convince the jury that his actions stemmed from “blind love” and financial disputes with Chow.

The judge said Lo stabbed Chow out of anger, hatred, and jealousy, and “perhaps it was nothing about love at all.” If he really loved her, the judge added, he should have spared her life.

Citing testimony from government forensic pathologist Gary Ying, the judge noted that Chow had sustained 43 knife wounds, with the deepest reaching 15 centimetres.

The defendant placed Chow inside a bathtub and changed his clothes before leaving the hotel, the judge said, calling his actions calm and deliberate.

He also did not tell the truth during the trial, instead claiming that he stabbed Chow after being provoked by her in a bid to lessen his offence, the judge said.

Chow was 23 when she died. She had been scheduled to fly to the US for a yoga training course when her body was found in the hotel bathtub on June 30, 2022.

The court heard during the trial that Lo and Chow became a couple in February 2021 and broke up the following January, although they stayed in touch.

Lo testified that he had run up enormous debt taking Chow to high-end restaurants and purchasing luxury items for her, saying he loved her very much. The debt left him suicidal, he said, as loan companies chased him to repay the money.

The West Bengal Chief Electoral Officer’s (CEO) office announced on Friday (November 20, 2026) the postponement of the Special Summary Revision (SSR) of the Photo Electoral Roll, 2027, which was scheduled to commence on November 23. The CEO’s office, in a statement, added that the decision has been taken due to “unavoidable circumstances.” The revised schedule for the exercise will be intimated subsequently, the statement said.

“The upcoming programme of Special Summary Revision of Photo Electoral Roll, which was scheduled from 23 November 2026 onwards, is hereby postponed due to some unavoidable circumstances,” the press statement said. As per the SSR schedule announced in the State, the publication of final electoral rolls is scheduled for January 2027.

The SSR, an annual exercise, usually seeks to enrol eligible voters—particularly young and first-time electors—and facilitate advance applications from those who will become eligible on April 1, July 1, and October 1, 2027. However, it had not been carried out after the SIR was launched last year.

The development comes ahead of pending civic elections in West Bengal. The state government is keen to hold elections to the civic bodies of Howrah and Kolkata. The Calcutta High Court had stayed elections to the Kolkata Municipal Corporation on the grounds that the challenge to the delimitation of wards of the civic body should be addressed by the Court before elections are declared.

The SSR will not come to the aid of the 38 lakh electors whose fate is pending before SIR tribunals after their names were removed from the voter list. According to an affidavit filed by the ECI in September earlier this year, of the 27 lakh electors who were excluded from the electoral rolls on the ground of “logical discrepancies,” 22 lakh voters have filed appeals before the tribunal challenging their exclusion. The EC’s affidavit also added that 16.10 lakh appeals have been filed against inclusions during SIR. This puts the total number of appeals of 38 lakh electors pending before the SIR tribunals.

Article 82 of the Constitution will come into force and delimitation will be held once the results of the ongoing Census exercise are out early next year. | Photo Credit: Sushil Kumar Verma

The Congress party on Friday said it favoured resolving the issue of delimitation through consultations with all political parties, but accused the government of making no effort to engage the Opposition on the matter.

Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said the party’s position was guided by a four-point formula: retaining the existing strength of 543 seats in the Lok Sabha; maintaining the present State-wise distribution of seats; reserving one-third (182) of the existing seats for women; and imposing a 25-year freeze on all three arrangements.

Mr. Ramesh said the need for an early consensus on the issue had become more pressing in view of of the fact that Article 82 of the Constitution will come into force and delimitation would be held once the results of the ongoing Census exercise are out early next year.

This could be unfavourable to some southern states – which have made progress in population control – and hence not feasible, he added.

Mr. Ramesh said the Congress was not opposed to delimitation as such, but believed that the exercise should not place any State at a disadvantage.

The Congress leader claimed that all parties in the INDIA bloc, including the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) and the Nationalist Congress Party (Sharadchandra Pawar), were on the same page on the four-point formula.

The DMK, he said, was also party to a resolution opposing any change in the number of Lok Sabha seats and seeking safeguards to ensure that Tamil Nadu was not disadvantaged by delimitation.

The Congress leader said seeking consultation was necessary because the government had not initiated any meaningful engagement with the Opposition.

He claimed that as per his information, the government has not shared a concrete proposal on delimitation even with constituents of the National Democratic Alliance.

The Congress wanted the matter to be discussed with all political parties and stakeholders to arrive at a consensus, Mr. Ramesh added.

The Monsoon session of Parliament has remained unprorogued since both Houses were adjourned sine die on August 13.

The decision has fuelled speculation about the possibility of the government convening Parliament at short notice to consider the proposed constitutional changes linked to women’s reservation and delimitation.

An extended or special sitting within the same session requires a minimum notice of two days, while convening a fresh session requires at least 14 days’ notice.

Speculation also continues over the timing of the winter session. Parliament has not held a winter session on four occasions: in 1975, 1979, 1984 and 2020.

items.title: Urban Forest Opens in Front of JR Osaka Station
items.summary: A new urban forest featuring waterfalls, ponds, and seasonal greenery opened on November 20 in the redevelopment district north of JR Osaka Station, creating an 8,400-square-meter oasis in the heart of the city's bustling Umeda district. (News On Japan)

scraped.title: Urban Forest Opens in Front of JR Osaka Station
scraped.description: A new urban forest featuring waterfalls, ponds, and seasonal greenery opened on November 20 in the redevelopment district north of JR Osaka Station, creating an 8,400-square-meter oasis in the heart of the city
scraped.author: News On Japan
scraped.h1: Urban Forest Opens in Front of JR Osaka Station
scraped.body_text:
OSAKA - A new urban forest featuring waterfalls, ponds, and seasonal greenery opened on November 20 in the redevelopment district north of JR Osaka Station, creating an 8,400-square-meter oasis in the heart of the city's bustling Umeda district.

Known as "Umekita Forest," the new attraction forms part of Grand Green Osaka, a major redevelopment project designed to bring nature into one of western Japan's busiest commercial centers. Surrounded by high-rise buildings and shopping complexes, including Grand Front Osaka, the forest offers visitors an unusually open view of the sky and a place to relax away from the surrounding streets. The forest, which officially opened at noon, was developed with New York's Central Park in Manhattan as a model, aiming to create a green retreat where residents, office workers, and tourists can enjoy nature throughout the year. A variety of trees are being planted to provide seasonal attractions, including cherry blossoms in spring and colorful maple leaves from late November through early December. Water features, including a flowing waterfall symbolizing Osaka's identity as a city of waterways, add to the natural atmosphere. The opening also marks the full completion of a 350-meter pedestrian walkway known as "Hirameki no Michi," or "Path of Inspiration," connecting the newly opened forest in the northern section of Grand Green Osaka with a popular lawn plaza to the south that opened two years ago. The walkway was designed to encourage visitors to discover new ideas and inspiration through encounters with nature and outdoor experiences, while providing a convenient pedestrian connection between the development's northern and southern areas. Wild birds, including Japanese white-eyes, have already been spotted in the forest, suggesting that the newly established green space is beginning to attract wildlife despite its location in central Osaka. With its combination of woodland scenery, seasonal flowers, autumn foliage, and flowing water, Umekita Forest is expected to become a popular destination for leisurely walks, relaxation, and outdoor recreation, offering a natural retreat within walking distance of one of Japan's busiest railway stations.

11月20日，位于JR大阪站北侧再开发区域的全新城市森林“梅北森林”正式开放，园内设有瀑布、池塘和四季各具特色的绿化景观，为繁华的大阪梅田中心地带增添了一片占地约8400平方米的城市绿洲。

items.title: Artwork Vandalized at Kyoto's Takase River Festival
items.summary: A series of vandalism incidents at an outdoor art exhibition along Kyoto's Takase River has left organizers shocked, with artworks repeatedly destroyed or removed since the festival opened on November 7, prompting a police investigation into suspected property damage. (News On Japan)

scraped.title: Artwork Vandalized at Kyoto
scraped.description: A series of vandalism incidents at an outdoor art exhibition along Kyoto
scraped.author: News On Japan
scraped.h1: Artwork Vandalized at Kyoto's Takase River Festival
scraped.body_text:
KYOTO - A series of vandalism incidents at an outdoor art exhibition along Kyoto's Takase River has left organizers shocked, with artworks repeatedly destroyed or removed since the festival opened on November 7, prompting a police investigation into suspected property damage.

The Takase River Art Festival features approximately 30 works displayed along the river that runs through central Kyoto. The exhibition was organized to give pedestrians an opportunity to encounter art unexpectedly while walking through the city, but several installations have become targets of deliberate destruction. The latest incident occurred on November 18, when an artwork resembling the American flag and bearing the satirical message "We Are Right" was removed from its display site. The piece, mounted on a heavy wooden panel measuring approximately 90 centimeters by 180 centimeters, was reportedly carried away by an unidentified person who shouted abusive remarks at people nearby. According to Tetsuro Fujimori, chairman of the festival's executive committee, witnesses reported seeing someone remove the artwork at around 2:30 p.m. The piece was subsequently discovered abandoned on the ground floor of a nearby building, while the person responsible had disappeared. At the original display site, concrete blocks that had supported the artwork were left piled haphazardly, with a message board buried beneath them. Fujimori expressed disbelief at the incident, describing the removal of an entire artwork as unprecedented. "It happened so suddenly. The idea that an artwork could simply disappear is something we have never experienced before. It is astonishing and outrageous," he said. The American flag installation was not the first work to suffer damage. Another piece, a circular installation designed to resemble the moon, has been deliberately broken on three separate occasions since the exhibition began. The first damage was discovered around November 7, shortly after the festival opened. Organizers repaired the artwork and returned it to its original location, only to discover that it had been damaged again on November 11. Although a person subsequently came forward and admitted responsibility for that incident, the artwork was vandalized for a third time on November 13. The circular piece was split through its center in a cross-shaped pattern, leaving it so badly damaged that its original appearance was almost unrecognizable. "It has been destroyed so severely that anyone looking at it would hardly recognize it as a work of art," Fujimori said. Visitors to the exhibition expressed anger and disappointment over the repeated attacks. "There really are heartless people. It's awful. I feel sorry for the artists," one visitor said. Another questioned why anyone would deliberately destroy the installations, describing the damage as appalling and saying it made them angry. The festival was intended to achieve more than simply displaying artwork. Organizers had hoped the installations would broaden public interest in art while contributing to improvements in the surrounding Kiyamachi district. Working with local residents, the executive committee sought to use art to improve neighborhood safety and discourage littering, helping create a more welcoming environment along the river. Fujimori said the repeated vandalism had undermined those efforts and caused considerable distress to the artists whose works were targeted. "By placing artworks along the Takase River, we wanted to make art more accessible to everyone," he said. "We also hoped that working with local people would help improve safety in Kiyamachi and discourage littering through the power of art." He emphasized that the damage went far beyond the physical destruction of the installations. "For an artist, a work of art is like an extension of themselves. This truly hurts them. I want to continue saying that such acts are an insult to art." The executive committee has filed a police report concerning the repeated destruction of the moon-shaped installation, and police are investigating the incidents as suspected property damage. The identity and motives of those responsible for the attacks remain unclear, leaving organizers concerned about the safety of the remaining artworks at an exhibition originally intended to bring art closer to the public.

items.title: Honda Unveils New Avancier SUV for Spring 2027 Launch
items.summary: Honda unveiled its new Avancier SUV on November 20th, marking its entry into the large SUV segment with a three-row hybrid model scheduled to go on sale in Japan in spring 2027 as part of a broader effort to revive its automobile business. (News On Japan)

scraped.title: Honda Unveils New Avancier SUV for Spring 2027 Launch
scraped.description: Honda unveiled its new Avancier SUV on November 20th, marking its entry into the large SUV segment with a three-row hybrid model scheduled to go on sale in Japan in spring 2027 as part of a broader effort to revive its automobile business.
scraped.author: News On Japan
scraped.h1: Honda Unveils New Avancier SUV for Spring 2027 Launch
scraped.body_text:
TOKYO - Honda unveiled its new Avancier SUV on November 20th, marking its entry into the large SUV segment with a three-row hybrid model scheduled to go on sale in Japan in spring 2027 as part of a broader effort to revive its automobile business.

The Avancier fills a gap in Honda's existing lineup, introducing a large SUV equipped with a newly developed hybrid system. The model is designed to strengthen the automaker's competitiveness in a segment where it has previously lacked a vehicle of this size. Honda plans to launch 15 hybrid models worldwide by fiscal 2029 as it seeks to rebuild its struggling automobile operations. The Avancier will be the first model introduced under this strategy, reflecting the company's growing emphasis on hybrid technology. In addition to its planned Japanese launch around spring 2027, Honda intends to sell the Avancier in overseas markets, including Thailand, China and Australia, as it expands its global hybrid vehicle lineup.

Japan's Nikkei 225 plunged 3,008 points, or 5.06%, to close at 56,437 on Friday, November 20, its lowest level in more than seven months, as a global selloff in artificial intelligence and semiconductor stocks swept through Tokyo following a disappointing market reaction to Anthropic's initial public offering in the United States, triggering widespread selling that extended to banks, consumer stocks and other major industries.

Japan Tobacco (JT) has announced that it will exclude seven companies involved in its Russian operations from its consolidated financial statements after the Russian government placed the businesses under temporary administration, with the Japanese tobacco giant expecting to record losses of approximately 1.377 trillion yen.

Tokyo stocks closed higher on Thursday, November 19, 2026, with the Nikkei 225 gaining 419.93 points, or 0.71%, to finish at 59,444.21 at the 3:30 p.m. close, extending its rebound for a second consecutive session as expectations surrounding the record-breaking initial public offering of U.S. artificial intelligence developer Anthropic supported selected technology shares, although declines in Nvidia, copper prices and smaller growth stocks exposed continuing weakness across the broader market.

Japan's core machinery orders fell 0.3% in September from the previous month to 1.0662 trillion yen, marking the first decline in two months, although the government maintained its assessment that orders are showing signs of recovery.

Japan's Nikkei 225 rebounded on November 18 after two consecutive days of losses, closing 163.85 points higher, or 0.28%, at 59,024.28 at 3:30 p.m. Tokyo time, although an early rally driven by strong earnings from U.S. chipmaker Nvidia quickly lost momentum, leaving investors cautious about the outlook for artificial intelligence, technology valuations and the broader economy.

Japan recorded a trade deficit of 476.5 billion yen in October, marking the sixth consecutive month of red ink, as persistently high crude oil prices linked to prolonged instability in the Middle East pushed import costs higher, according to trade statistics released by the Finance Ministry on November 18th.
